reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA1 publishes 12.6 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that figure implies roughly 315 racks; at a more typical colocation density of 10 kW per rack it implies roughly 1,260 racks. NTT has not published a rack count, a power density ceiling, or a cooling architecture, so which assumption fits this facility is not determinable from the operator's own page.

Among the 20 Virginia facilities on this site that publish a megawatt figure, VA1 ranks 18th, contributing 12.6 MW of the 1,338.6 MW total, a share of approximately 0.9 percent. Virginia has 326 mapped facilities in total, meaning the large majority publish no capacity figure at all; the state total is almost certainly an undercount. VA1 is a mid-sized site in a state that holds more published data-center capacity than any other in the country, concentrated in the Ashburn corridor where VA1 itself sits.

No certifications are listed in the published specifications for this facility, so no statement about uptime tier or compliance posture can be made from the data. At 12.6 MW, VA1 is not a large-scale AI training campus by current standards, where hyperscale AI clusters routinely consume hundreds of megawatts. It could support inference workloads or smaller training runs, but the operator has not published the power density, redundancy, or network specifications that would confirm or rule out any particular AI use case.
